children: Australian shares extended losses on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected inflation data tempered hopes of rate cuts next year, dragging rate-sensitive financial stocks lower.
fell 0.7% to 8,663.5 by 0043 GMT, with only two sectors in positive territory. The benchmark rose 1.8% on Tuesday to snap an eight-session losing streak.
Data showed consumer prices climbed more than expected in October, while a stubbornly high reading for core inflation underlined why interest rates have risen five times this year.
Annual inflation rose to 4.9%, the fastest reading in the short life of the monthly series and well above the central bank's target band of 2%-3%.
Attention now shifts to the Reserve Bank of Australia's final meeting of the year in December. The central bank has raised interest rates by 125 basis points so far this year.

Interest-rate cuts could help revive consumer spending and lower borrowing costs.
